steps.text: Check the port is free first (`lsof -nP -iTCP:4321 -sTCP:LISTEN` must be empty — Astro silently hops ports when squatted, and you would be judging the wrong site); then run `pnpm registry:build && pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build` — exits 0 naming no violation offenders; stdout carries `[docs-data] changelog: 3 tags, 3 entries — one-to-one, reverse-chronological` and `[docs-data] guides: 5 guides — cap satisfied`; then `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs preview --port 4321` serves http://localhost:4321.   `exercises: GBC-005, GBC-007, GBC-011, GBC-012`
steps.evidence: Port 4321 was empty on attempt 2 (lsof exit 1, 0 bytes). Docs build exit 0. Both [docs-data] lines present. link-check 0 errors. Preview served http://localhost:4321/ HTTP 200.

steps.text: Open http://localhost:4321/docs/owns-vs-does-not-own, http://localhost:4321/porting, and http://localhost:4321/registry. On the boundary page read the ships/does-not-ship table (`transport`, `streaming client`, `tool executor` in does-not-ship cells; `useChat` in the consumer-wires cell) and the ownership-split + gaps table. On /porting read the mapping table (a deviations column, ≥5 rows) and the not-ported list. On /registry confirm exactly 56 rows split 39/11/6. Cross-check: every boundary gap is a consumer-owned responsibility or a named not-ported upstream element — zero contradictions, zero known omissions.   `exercises: GBC-003, GBC-004, GBC-006, GBC-017`
steps.evidence: Boundary does-not-ship cells name transport, streaming client, and tool executor; useChat is in the consumer cell. Porting deviations column, 41 mapping rows, 9 not-ported. Registry 56 = 39/11/6. Gap names are consumer responsibilities, not the not-ported list.

steps.text: First contact — on your own machine, in your own clone as it is (no fixture, no seeded data, no HOME override, no locked flow), start the docs site the way CONTRIBUTING.md documents: from the repository root run `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs build`, then `pnpm --filter @rnr-ai-elements/docs preview`, and open the URL that preview prints (Astro's default is http://localhost:4321; use whatever port it reports). The build's own output under apps/docs/dist/ is the only thing written; stop before any other write (no install, no publish, no edits to files). Promise (UC-DOCS-03): "A Guides section capped at five launch pages serves the re-theme, update, preview, engine-choice, and port-next jobs without becoming a curriculum." Promise (UC-DOCS-04): "The boundary page states as scannable tables that the library ships no transport, no streaming client, and no tool executor, and points to the example app as the worked reference." Promise (UC-DOCS-05): "Porting notes explain intentional divergences from Vercel AI Elements and earlier RN ports before an extender backports anything." Promise (UC-DOCS-06): "One entry per release in reverse chronological order makes maintenance health visible on the site." Then see, on THIS machine: the build exits 0, the preview serves the printed URL, and the header links Guides, Porting, and Changelog each open a real page (not a 404) that matches its promise above; if the printed port differs from 4321, judge the site at that port.   `exercises: GBC-013, GBC-009, GBC-010, GBC-004, GBC-008`
